//overrides: qs is the query-string parser Express hands every request to. Everything up to 6.15.3 has a
denial of service an attacker can trigger from a URL (GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g, GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx,
GHSA-q8mj-m7cp-5q26), and 6.16.0 is the fix. Express 4 pins ~6.14.0, so npm resolves a
vulnerable copy under node_modules/express no matter how often `npm audit fix` is run - it
reports a fix is available and then cannot apply one. The only other route npm offers is
`--force`, which upgrades Express to 5 and is a breaking change to a working server.
So the version is forced here instead. qs 6.14 -> 6.16 is a patch to parsing limits; Express
calls qs.parse for req.query and nothing else, and check-boot.js drives the real server with
the real Express, so `npm test` is a genuine check that this still works.
Revisit when Express 4 widens its own range, and delete this then.
//devDependencies: jsdoc generates the doclet dump the Docs tab is built from. It is NOT used at runtime and is
not needed to run the app — only to re-run `npm run build:docs`, whose output is committed.
It is here because phaser's own types/phaser.json, which ships on npm, is missing two
namespaces its website shows: Phaser's docs build drops @ignore'd doclets. See
tools/build-phaser-doclets.js. Pinned to 3.x because that is what Phaser's own build uses.
